Our Pi Mensae light curve draws on TESS sectors 1, 4, 8, 11 (confirmed via the lightkurve search results, same selection order download_lc() uses), spanning BTJD 1330.0-1613.6. Checked against BLS's own 27.21 d period (not Pi Men c's real period): event 1 (SNR 15.62, depth 1059 ppm) folds to -301.94 h -> out-of-transit; event 2 (SNR 15.56, depth 842 ppm) folds to -247.83 h -> out-of-transit. A mismatch here reflects BLS locking onto a different (likely aliased) period rather than necessarily meaning ExoVeil is wrong. Cross-checked instead against the refined Pi Men c ephemeris of Larsen et al. (2026, arXiv:2607.12088, "TESS Photometry and Radial Velocity Analysis of the sub-Neptune Exoplanet Pi Mensae c...", Table 2; 20 TESS sectors S1-S95): P=6.267823±1e-06 d, T0=1325.5042±0.0003 BTJD, T14=2.969 h -- top-2: event 1 folds to -50.81 h -> out-of-transit; event 2 folds to -55.97 h -> out-of-transit. Extending to **all 20 returned events**: 0/20 land in-transit. Ephemeris-uncertainty check: propagating T0/P uncertainty (N_cycles x sigma_P, quadrature with sigma_T0) out to our most-distant event (46.0 cycles from T0) gives a timing uncertainty of only 0.44 min (0.49% of the ±1.48 h half-duration window) using the refined ephemeris -- vs. 1.13 min with the prior (pre-2607.12088, ~10x larger period-error) solution. Even the OLD ephemeris was already precise enough here; the refined one makes the margin larger still. Since the propagated uncertainty is <1% of the search window, the near-total absence of in-transit events (0-1/20 depending on ephemeris used, vs. top-2 SNR ~15.6/15.6) is NOT an ephemeris-precision artifact -- it stands as a genuine non-detection of a known, previously-confirmed planet by ExoVeil at threshold=5.0 in this run, not just a top-event mismatch.

EB (P=0.66d) outside ExoVeil's validated regime. Top event's raw SNR (1.086e+07) is a numerical artifact, not a real detection significance: exoveil.detect.detect_events() weights residuals by 1/local_MAD(residual); the EB's sharp, near-total eclipse drives the local MAD toward ~0 in that window, blowing up the ratio. Second-ranked event (SNR=62.0, t=3528.67 BTJD) is a more representative 'top' detection for this target -- included in all_events for reference. That 2nd-ranked event folds to -0.53 h from transit center -> out-of-transit. Illustrates the single-transit matched filter breaking numerically on non-planet, high-contrast periodic signals.
